answer: Let \(P\) be the transition matrix for bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph; voting weight comes from propagated trust, not raw identities. Given fixed trusted seed mass and bounded degrees, a sybil cluster with a sparse external cut has low conductance: few walks enter it, so cut-based bounds limit its aggregate weight despite dense internal links. A pearl of trusted attestations can therefore resist a tide of fabricated accounts; marble-like connectivity within the cluster does not create trust.
